scenes.headline: Silver Layer
scenes.subtitle: Cleaned, conformed, and enriched data
scenes.narration: The silver layer refines raw bronze data into validated, structured, and joined tables ready for analysis.

scenes.headline: What silver does
items: Deduplicate and handle nulls and bad records
Enrich by joining reference and dimension data
scenes.narration: Silver turns messy raw input into clean, typed columns. It removes duplicates and quarantines invalid rows so data quality is trustworthy. Joining reference data adds the context that analysts need.

scenes.headline: Bronze to silver transformation
scenes.narration: We read the raw bronze table and apply schema and validation rules. Duplicates are removed and records are enriched with lookups. The result is written as a clean silver Delta table.

scenes.headline: Building a silver table
scenes.code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, to_timestamp

bronze = spark.readStream.table("bronze.clickstream_events")

silver = (bronze
    .filter(col("user_id").isNotNull())
    .withColumn("event_ts", to_timestamp("event_time"))
    .dropDuplicates(["event_id"])
    .join(spark.table("ref.users"), "user_id", "left"))

(silver.writeStream
    .option("checkpointLocation", "/chk/silver_clickstream")
    .table("silver.clickstream_enriched"))
scenes.narration: We read from bronze and drop rows missing a user identifier. Timestamps are cast to proper types and duplicate events are removed. A left join with the user reference table enriches each event before writing to silver.

scenes.headline: Why silver matters
items: Provides a single, trusted, query-ready dataset
Isolates cleansing logic from raw ingestion
Serves both analysts and machine learning
scenes.narration: Silver gives the organization one consistent version of clean data. Separating cleansing from ingestion keeps each layer focused. Well-formed silver tables feed dashboards and models alike.

scenes.text: Silver is the enterprise's clean, conformed, single version of the truth.
scenes.narration: Most self-service analytics and feature engineering should read from silver, not raw bronze.
